significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that the measurable "Conservation-Invariance Score" is predictively coupled to "downstream physical-consistency errors," with sensitivity increasing with violation magnitude; this would constrain which conservation laws a model will fail on rather than merely show that a quantity is decodable. It establishes a behavioral phenomenon and a structured internal geometric account, but not a causal mechanism, since the claim expressly describes the downstream link as correlational; this matters where work such as Bronstein et al.'s Geometric Deep Learning framework and E(3)-equivariant models treats symmetry as an architectural design constraint. The branches are determinate: failure of the preserving-versus-violating displacement contrast or of the CIS-error coupling would rule out this proposed geometry as a general read-only proxy, although it would not rule out other encodings of conservation. In the topic-substitution check, a generic proposal to probe scientific concepts would merit only the topic median, whereas the quoted cross-law predictive coupling and graded "monotone response to violation magnitude" are specific constraints absent from that baseline.

reach.justification: The named handle is the "Conservation-Invariance Score," offered as a "read-only diagnostic that predicts where the model produces physically inconsistent outputs" and as a per-law model audit. This is potentially ex ante at the law or model level—an auditor could identify weak conservation principles before deployment—although it does not clearly forecast individual failures before their inputs are attempted. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction low CIS implies greater downstream inconsistency still transfers as a relation, and the hypothesis asserts model-agnostic scope across molecular, protein, and materials models, making auditors and model builders plausible downstream users. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: the broad scientific-representation topic alone supplies neither this transferable predictor nor the stated action window.
